primary_sources: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications

rules.explanation: Giving AI agents unrestricted code execution or write permissions to databases without approval can lead to severe data loss or system corruption.
rules.do: Execute autonomous tools inside isolated sandboxes (e.g., Docker, E2B) and enforce Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval for destructive actions.
rules.dont: Do not give LLM agents direct, unmonitored execution access to production databases or host shell environments.

rules.explanation: Malicious user input or untrusted third-party data can hijack system instructions (Direct/Indirect Prompt Injection) and leak system prompts or sensitive data.
rules.do: Implement defensive input validation, output sanitization, and safety guardrails (e.g., NeMo Guardrails, Llama Guard).
rules.dont: Do not pass raw, unvalidated external web scraping outputs or untrusted inputs directly into privileged system prompts.

rules.rule_name: Multi-Agent State Management and Loop Prevention
rules.explanation: In multi-agent systems, cyclic reasoning loops between agents can cause infinite token consumption and system deadlocks.
rules.do: Define explicit state graphs (e.g., LangGraph state schemas) with maximum step limits and termination conditions.
rules.dont: Do not deploy multi-agent communication networks without hard recursion limits and explicit cycle termination triggers.

rules.explanation: Unchecked generative outputs can present fabricated facts or incorrect references as truth, eroding trust in production systems.
rules.do: Incorporate automated factuality checking, grounding metrics, and fallback disclosures when confidence scores drop below thresholds.
rules.dont: Do not allow models to present authoritative claims without verifying grounding against retrieved context or deterministic logic.
